Definition: a scorpion; figuratively, a scourge or knotted whip
BiblicalUsage: A scorpion is the desert's sting, and it becomes the picture of a scourge. Moses reminds Israel that God led them through a wilderness of fiery serpents and scorpions; Ezekiel is told not to fear, though he dwells among scorpions; and Rehoboam threatens that his father chastised with whips, but he will chastise with scorpions.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God lets His people walk among scorpions and still keeps them. A king who reaches for the scorpion instead of the staff has already lost his kingdom.
